diagnosis.what_happened: Paragraph alignment in Word deliverables was visually broken or defaulted to Left in Microsoft Word despite BiDi being set.
diagnosis.behavior_caused_outcome: Manually appending <w:jc> to <w:pPr> placed it after <w:rPr>, violating ECMA-376 schema sequence and causing Word to ignore the alignment. Furthermore, adding headings as Normal paragraphs caused post-fixers to misclassify them and apply Justify instead of Right.
diagnosis.what_should_have_happened: Always use python-docx native p.alignment (WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT, CENTER, JUSTIFY) which places <w:jc> in valid schema position before <w:rPr>, and assign explicit heading styles.
diagnosis.rationale_why: Microsoft Word strictly requires valid OpenXML child sequence in <w:pPr>; out-of-order children are silently discarded by the Word rendering engine.

desired_behavior: Use python-docx native enums (p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT/CENTER/JUSTIFY) and never append loose <w:jc> tags at the end of <w:pPr>.
generalization: OpenXML Schema Alignment Invariant: All paragraph alignments in python-docx must be set via native p.alignment properties to maintain ECMA-376 child element ordering before <w:rPr>.
